messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

Source link: https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/3e68/c4204aa7be83590b2fbb4e51db36dcdc64f3.pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1007/s10404-007-0161-8

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Open-Surface Digital Microfluidic Potentiometric/Conductometric Titration

REAGENTS USED:
  - Analyte solution (sample droplet, created from an on-chip analyte reservoir)
  - Titrant solution (diluent droplet, created from an on-chip titrant reservoir)

STEPS:
1-2. Droplet creation: Create one droplet from the analyte reservoir and one droplet from the titrant reservoir.
3-4. Splitting: Split each of the two droplets into two smaller droplets.
5-6. First merge: Merge one analyte half with one titrant half to form a 50:50 mixture; return the unused titrant half to the reservoir.
7. Mixing: Mix the merged 50:50 droplet by rotating it clockwise then counterclockwise over four grid electrodes.
8. First split-for-detection: Split the mixed 50:50 droplet into two. Send one half to the detection site to record its pH or conductivity reading.
9. Second dilution: Merge the retained half with a fresh analyte droplet to form a 75:25 (analyte:titrant) mixture; mix by rotation and split again.
10. Second split-for-detection: Send one half to the detection site to record its pH or conductivity reading; create and split another fresh analyte droplet.
11. Third dilution: Merge the retained half with the fresh analyte droplet to form an 88:12 (analyte:titrant) mixture.
12. Final detection: Send the resulting droplet to the detection site to record its pH or conductivity reading.

INTERPRETATION: The protocol demonstrates that serial dilution/titration -- normally requiring continuous titrant addition on a benchtop potentiometer or conductometer -- can instead be reprogrammed as a sequence of droplet splitting, merging, and rotational mixing steps on an open-surface digital microfluidic array. Each detection-site reading (pH or conductivity) at the 50:50, 75:25, and 88:12 dilution stages allows the assay to be halted once the target endpoint is reached, illustrating the reprogrammability advantage of open-surface droplet manipulation over fixed-channel or continuous-flow microfluidics.

module fluorescence

manifest analyte
manifest titrant

instructions:

a1 = dispense 5 units of analyte
t1 = dispense 5 units of titrant
mix_50 = mix a1 with t1 for 30s

reading_50 = detect fluorescence on mix_50 for 10s

if (reading_50 <= 40) {
    dispose mix_50

    a2 = dispense 8 units of analyte
    t2 = dispense 2 units of titrant
    mix_75 = mix a2 with t2 for 30s

    reading_75 = detect fluorescence on mix_75 for 10s

    if (reading_75 <= 40) {
        dispose mix_75

        a3 = dispense 9 units of analyte
        t3 = dispense 1 units of titrant
        mix_88 = mix a3 with t3 for 30s

        reading_88 = detect fluorescence on mix_88 for 10s
        dispose mix_88
    }
}

identity.protocol_name: Potentiometric/Conductometric Titration on Open-Surface Digital Microfluidics (Yoon, 2008)

chemical_evidence.source_quote: Two drops are created from analyte and titrant reservoirs
titrant should continuously be added to an analyte

operation_evidence.bs_operation: mix_50 = mix a1 with t1 for 30s
operation_evidence.source_quote: described as merging sample and diluent 50:50, then mixing by rotation
one split-merged drop is sent to the detection site to record its pH or conductivity
the other half is merged with sample to get 75:25 mixing
the other half is merged with sample to get 88:12 mixing

numeric_mismatches.note: The paper's protocol explicitly splits droplets into halves at each stage (Fig. 9); BioScript's confirmed grammar has no authored 'split' keyword, so each post-split ratio is instead approximated via a fresh weighted dispense (5:5, 8:2, 9:1) rather than a literal split of a prior droplet.

Detection in the paper is potentiometric (pH meter) or conductometric, not fluorescent. 'fluorescence' is used only because it is the sole detect module confirmed working in the reference BioScript files; it stands in for a generic quantitative pH/conductivity signal read.

The paper does not specify a numeric pH/conductivity endpoint value; 40 is a placeholder threshold used to demonstrate the iterative refine-until-endpoint control flow described qualitatively in the text, and should be replaced with the analyte's real target reading.

numeric_mismatches.field: grid rotation, four-grid CW/CCW mixing pattern
numeric_mismatches.note: The paper describes mixing via rotation over four grid electrodes, clockwise then counterclockwise; BioScript has no primitive for spatial rotation patterns, so this is folded into a plain 'mix ... for 30s' with no positional detail.

metadata.notes: This protocol details Open-Surface Digital Microfluidic Potentiometric/Conductometric Titration. The assay is performed on a Digital Microfluidics (DMF) platform. Key reagents used in the assay include Analyte solution and Titrant solution.
